005package org.wpilib.system;
006
007import static org.wpilib.units.Units.Seconds;
008
009import java.io.Closeable;
010import java.util.PriorityQueue;
011import java.util.concurrent.locks.ReentrantLock;
012import org.wpilib.driverstation.DriverStationErrors;
013import org.wpilib.hardware.hal.HALUtil;
014import org.wpilib.hardware.hal.NotifierJNI;
015import org.wpilib.units.measure.Time;
016import org.wpilib.util.WPIUtilJNI;
017
018/**
019 * A class that's a wrapper around a watchdog timer.
020 *
021 * <p>When the timer expires, a message is printed to the console and an optional user-provided
022 * callback is invoked.
023 *
024 * <p>The watchdog is initialized disabled, so the user needs to call enable() before use.
025 */
026public class Watchdog implements Closeable, Comparable<Watchdog> {
027  // Used for timeout print rate-limiting
028  private static final long MIN_PRINT_PERIOD = 1_000_000_000L; // ns
029
030  // Monotonic times in nanoseconds. Seconds in a double can't hold
031  // nanosecond-resolution timestamps once the clock is large.
032  private long m_startTime;
033  private double m_timeout;
034  private long m_expirationTime;
035  private final Runnable m_callback;
036  private long m_lastTimeoutPrint; // ns
037
038  boolean m_isExpired;
039
040  boolean m_suppressTimeoutMessage;
041
042  private final Tracer m_tracer;
043
044  private static final PriorityQueue<Watchdog> m_watchdogs = new PriorityQueue<>();
045  private static ReentrantLock m_queueMutex = new ReentrantLock();
046  private static int m_notifier;
047
048  static {
049    m_notifier = NotifierJNI.createNotifier();
050    NotifierJNI.setNotifierName(m_notifier, "Watchdog");
051    startDaemonThread(Watchdog::schedulerFunc);
052  }
053
054  /**
055   * Watchdog constructor.
056   *
057   * @param timeout The watchdog's timeout in seconds with nanosecond resolution.
058   * @param callback This function is called when the timeout expires.
059   */
060  public Watchdog(double timeout, Runnable callback) {
061    m_timeout = timeout;
062    m_callback = callback;
063    m_tracer = new Tracer();
064  }
065
066  /**
067   * Watchdog constructor.
068   *
069   * @param timeout The watchdog's timeout with nanosecond resolution.
070   * @param callback This function is called when the timeout expires.
071   */
072  public Watchdog(Time timeout, Runnable callback) {
073    this(timeout.in(Seconds), callback);
074  }
075
076  @Override
077  public void close() {
078    disable();
079  }
080
081  @Override
082  public boolean equals(Object obj) {
083    return obj instanceof Watchdog watchdog && m_expirationTime == watchdog.m_expirationTime;
084  }
085
086  @Override
087  public int hashCode() {
088    return Long.hashCode(m_expirationTime);
089  }
090
091  @Override
092  public int compareTo(Watchdog rhs) {
093    // Elements with sooner expiration times are sorted as lesser. The head of
094    // Java's PriorityQueue is the least element.
095    return Long.compare(m_expirationTime, rhs.m_expirationTime);
096  }
097
098  /**
099   * Returns the time in seconds since the watchdog was last fed.
100   *
101   * @return The time in seconds since the watchdog was last fed.
102   */
103  public double getTime() {
104    return (HALUtil.getMonotonicTime() - m_startTime) / 1e9;
105  }
106
107  /**
108   * Sets the watchdog's timeout.
109   *
110   * @param timeout The watchdog's timeout in seconds with nanosecond resolution.
111   */
112  public void setTimeout(double timeout) {
113    m_startTime = HALUtil.getMonotonicTime();
114    m_tracer.clearEpochs();
115
116    m_queueMutex.lock();
117    try {
118      m_timeout = timeout;
119      m_isExpired = false;
120
121      m_watchdogs.remove(this);
122      m_expirationTime = m_startTime + Math.round(m_timeout * 1e9);
123      m_watchdogs.add(this);
124      updateAlarm();
125    } finally {
126      m_queueMutex.unlock();
127    }
128  }
129
130  /**
131   * Returns the watchdog's timeout in seconds.
132   *
133   * @return The watchdog's timeout in seconds.
134   */
135  public double getTimeout() {
136    m_queueMutex.lock();
137    try {
138      return m_timeout;
139    } finally {
140      m_queueMutex.unlock();
141    }
142  }
143
144  /**
145   * Returns true if the watchdog timer has expired.
146   *
147   * @return True if the watchdog timer has expired.
148   */
149  public boolean isExpired() {
150    m_queueMutex.lock();
151    try {
152      return m_isExpired;
153    } finally {
154      m_queueMutex.unlock();
155    }
156  }
157
158  /**
159   * Adds time since last epoch to the list printed by printEpochs().
160   *
161   * @see Tracer#addEpoch(String)
162   * @param epochName The name to associate with the epoch.
163   */
164  public void addEpoch(String epochName) {
165    m_tracer.addEpoch(epochName);
166  }
167
168  /**
169   * Prints list of epochs added so far and their times.
170   *
171   * @see Tracer#printEpochs()
172   */
173  public void printEpochs() {
174    m_tracer.printEpochs();
175  }
176
177  /**
178   * Resets the watchdog timer.
179   *
180   * <p>This also enables the timer if it was previously disabled.
181   */
182  public void reset() {
183    enable();
184  }
185
186  /** Enables the watchdog timer. */
187  public void enable() {
188    m_startTime = HALUtil.getMonotonicTime();
189    m_tracer.clearEpochs();
190
191    m_queueMutex.lock();
192    try {
193      m_isExpired = false;
194
195      m_watchdogs.remove(this);
196      m_expirationTime = m_startTime + Math.round(m_timeout * 1e9);
197      m_watchdogs.add(this);
198      updateAlarm();
199    } finally {
200      m_queueMutex.unlock();
201    }
202  }
203
204  /** Disables the watchdog timer. */
205  public void disable() {
206    m_queueMutex.lock();
207    try {
208      m_watchdogs.remove(this);
209      updateAlarm();
210    } finally {
211      m_queueMutex.unlock();
212    }
213  }
214
215  /**
216   * Enable or disable suppression of the generic timeout message.
217   *
218   * <p>This may be desirable if the user-provided callback already prints a more specific message.
219   *
220   * @param suppress Whether to suppress generic timeout message.
221   */
222  public void suppressTimeoutMessage(boolean suppress) {
223    m_suppressTimeoutMessage = suppress;
224  }
225
226  @SuppressWarnings("resource")
227  private static void updateAlarm() {
228    if (m_watchdogs.isEmpty()) {
229      NotifierJNI.cancelNotifierAlarm(m_notifier, true);
230    } else {
231      NotifierJNI.setNotifierAlarm(m_notifier, m_watchdogs.peek().m_expirationTime, 0, true, true);
232    }
233  }
234
235  private static Thread startDaemonThread(Runnable target) {
236    Thread inst = new Thread(target);
237    inst.setDaemon(true);
238    inst.start();
239    return inst;
240  }
241
242  private static void schedulerFunc() {
243    while (!Thread.currentThread().isInterrupted()) {
244      try {
245        WPIUtilJNI.waitForObject(m_notifier);
246      } catch (InterruptedException ex) {
247        Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
248        break;
249      }
250      long curTime = HALUtil.getMonotonicTime();
251
252      m_queueMutex.lock();
253      try {
254        if (m_watchdogs.isEmpty()) {
255          continue;
256        }
257
258        // If the condition variable timed out, that means a Watchdog timeout
259        // has occurred, so call its timeout function.
260        Watchdog watchdog = m_watchdogs.poll();
261
262        if (curTime - watchdog.m_lastTimeoutPrint > MIN_PRINT_PERIOD) {
263          watchdog.m_lastTimeoutPrint = curTime;
264          if (!watchdog.m_suppressTimeoutMessage) {
265            DriverStationErrors.reportWarning(
266                String.format("Watchdog not fed within %.6fs\n", watchdog.m_timeout), false);
267          }
268        }
269
270        // Set expiration flag before calling the callback so any
271        // manipulation of the flag in the callback (e.g., calling
272        // Disable()) isn't clobbered.
273        watchdog.m_isExpired = true;
274
275        m_queueMutex.unlock();
276        try {
277          watchdog.m_callback.run();
278        } finally {
279          m_queueMutex.lock();
280        }
281
282        updateAlarm();
283      } finally {
284        m_queueMutex.unlock();
285      }
286    }
287  }
288}
